县城贵妇 — the "county-town socialite" and the migration of consumption to lower-tier cities (fresh region off Korea 93/93.5, Indonesia 92, Vietnam 91; distinct subject from China's guzi 73 / Xiaohongshu 79)

"budol" — a street-swindle word reclaimed as a Gen-Z confession of overspending on TikTok Shop live-selling ("na-budol ako"/"mine wars"); consumer-culture/linguistic, distinct from the platform-as-state DSWD×TikTok (81) and "backing out of the feed" (76). Under-radar verified (no NYT/BBC/Reuters/FT feature). Off China(94)/Korea(93).

"joki" — the proxy economy: renting a competent stranger to perform an obligation (joki skripsi/game/Prakerja/Strava/vaksin); the argument is that proof has decoupled from achievement and a market fills the gap ("fix the box, not the jockey"). Under-radar verified (no NYT/BBC/Reuters/FT feature). Fresh region off China(94)/Philippines(95); distinct from Indonesia 92's recorded subject.

"Beli Sekarang, Bayar Kemudian" (BSBK / BNPL) — the mutation of Buy Now, Pay Later from an aspirational shopping toy into subsistence credit: Malaysians splitting sub-RM100 baskets of groceries, formula, fuel and phone bills into three (avg ticket ~RM91; 243m txns / RM21.3bn in 2025, +78% y/y; SPayLater/Atome/Grab >90% of users; 55% of one surveyed cohort have no other credit), and a brand-new regulator (Consumer Credit Act 2025 → Suruhanjaya Kredit Pengguna, live 1 Mar 2026) racing to license/affordability-check/bureau-report it before the crash. Argument = point-of-sale credit as privatised shadow welfare for the bank-excluded, the cost-of-living risk moved from the state's balance sheet to the household's; analogy = South Korea's 2003 credit-card crisis (regulate-before vs deregulate-into). Under-radar verified (no NYT/BBC/Reuters/FT feature; SCMP/BenarNews have run the youth-debt angle, not this thesis). Fresh region off China(94)/Philippines(95)/Indonesia(96)/Japan(97).

หมอลำ (mor lam) — the Isan folk-opera concert circuit as Thailand’s largest live-entertainment format and a ~6bn-baht branded media platform (MI Group; ~20m reached across ~2,600 shows in 2024, +127% vs the pre-COVID baseline); national FMCG brands (Osotspa M-150 “gold at every mor lam show,” four troupes) fight for “Isan purchasing power,” coining the marketing category ภูธรเอนเตอร์เทน (phuthon entertain, “upcountry entertainment”); digital pivot onto Facebook Live/TikTok (78.8% watch live+online). Argument = the consumption frontier is the poorest, most-populous region, not Bangkok; the boom is real but structurally thin (remittance-fed; Isan ~1/3 of population, ~1/10 of GDP). Analogy = luk thung / US country music (regional working-class music, stigma reversal, brand sponsorship, red-shirt political coding). Under-radar verified (no NYT/BBC/Reuters/FT/CNN/Guardian feature on the mor lam economy; Songlines world-music only). Sceptic = the govt PRD 6.6bn-baht / 40k-jobs figure sits inside a soft-power campaign (directional), and +127% is partly a COVID rebound. Fresh region off Malaysia(98)/Japan(97)/Indonesia(96); Thailand last = mutelu(84), distinct subject.

苦労キャンセル界隈 (kurō kyanseru kaiwai) — the "hardship-cancel sphere": online micro-communities (界隈) naming and monetising the public refusal to endure, from 風呂キャンセル界隈 "bath-cancel" (X, Apr 2024, 30k+ likes; ~40 variants incl. overtime-cancel by Sep 2025) to Nikkei Trendy's named 2026 forecast theme, where you pay money or offload to generative AI to erase hardship (fast passes, resignation agencies, chatbots). Argument = the collapse of the gaman (我慢) endurance ethic and effort repriced from virtue to exploitation on a labour shortage, with AI received as relief-from-suffering. Under-radar verified (no NYT/BBC/Reuters/FT/CNN/Guardian feature). Fresh region off Indonesia(96)/Philippines(95)/China(94); distinct from Japan nuikatsu(71)/malatang(83)/背徳グルメ(86) and from the proxy-economy joki(96) — nothing is faked here, endurance itself is repudiated.

存股族 (cún-gǔ-zú, the “stock-saving tribe”) and the 月月配 monthly-dividend high-dividend ETF economy — and its first crack in 2026. Taiwan financialised the paycheck: in a super-aged, wage-stagnant society with a distrusted pension, households manufacture a synthetic monthly salary from monthly-paying dividend ETFs (an income-SUBSCRIPTION product treated as a wage/DIY pension). 18m beneficiary accounts (per-fund, not unique; ~14.6m brokerage held); >60% of NT$3.9tn ETF assets in high-dividend; flagship 00940 (launch Mar 2024, NT$220bn/mo, crashed brokerages) lost ~251k beneficiaries (−44%) in 2026 while market-cap 0050 gained ~1.52m — trigger = high-div funds trailed a +56% index by 6–11pts and the retail crowd naming 吃老本 (return-of-capital dressed as income). Argument = when a society stops believing the wage/state will provide, financial products become emotional infrastructure. Analogy = Japan’s Mrs. Watanabe FX carry trade (~$9.1bn/day retail by 2007; capped 2010/11). Under-radar verified (only local/trade press — CommonWealth/Taipei Times/bnext/Newtalk — plus one Bloomberg 0050-flows markets item; no NYT/BBC/Reuters/FT/CNN/Guardian feature on the culture or its reversal). Sceptic = maturation-not-disillusionment (money rotated within the market; older div funds still gaining), the 18m-holdings stat is soft, and 吃老本 is a contested critique not a blanket fact. Fresh region off Thailand(99)/Malaysia(98)/Japan(97)/Indonesia(96)/Philippines(95)/China(94); Taiwan last = CPBL cheerleaders(74), distinct subject.

STREEDHAN (Stridhan) — the family-gold loan boom: Indian households pledging inherited women's gold at industrial scale as the shame flips from ruin to savvy finance. Households hold ~34,600t of gold (~$3.8tn, ~89% of GDP); loans against jewellery near ₹5.52 lakh crore (Jul 2026, ~2× a year earlier), the gold-loan book ~3.8× since 2022 = India's 2nd-largest retail credit product; women hold 43.5% of gold loans (the highest share of any credit product); gold >₹1,50,000/10g (index +144% in 2yr), avg ticket ~doubled. De-stigmatisation engineered (Muthoot "Sunheri Soch," Bachchan-narrated). Analogy = 1991 BoP crisis (67t pledged to the IMF, ~46.9t airlifted to BoE/BoJ, ~20t sold to UBS in a secret night repo). Argument = a society liquefying its most private, gendered, inheritance-bound RESERVE; the sovereign's 1991 shame is now household normalcy — financialisation of the sacred store-of-value, DISTINCT from Taiwan's synthetic-wage financialisation (100). Sceptic = definitional spread inflates growth (much is collateral revaluation + reclassified farm loans, per RBI), low delinquency may mask stress, "empowerment" may be distress, the distress figure (Kharge's 4cr women) is a political claim. Under-radar verified (no NYT/BBC/Reuters/FT/CNN/Guardian feature on the streedhan-as-collateral society angle; Reuters markets-wire figures + a CNBC newsletter only). Fresh region off Taiwan(100)/Thailand(99)/Malaysia(98)/Japan(97)/Indonesia(96)/Philippines(95)/China(94)/Korea(93); India last = astrology/faith-tech 68/72, distinct subject.

CHOP-CHOP — the normalised illicit-tobacco economy: the world’s toughest tobacco control (plain packaging 2012 + the highest excise on earth, lifted twice yearly by indexation) drove smoking to record lows and, past a tipping point, manufactured a parallel untaxed market. Illicit tobacco ~40% of national consumption (from ~28.6% a year earlier; some estimates >50%); ~80% of 18-24 purchases likely illicit (Cancer Council Generation Vape Wave 10, n=232); ~A$8-12bn/yr forgone excise; ~20,000 Sydney tobacconists (~60 per McDonald’s); legal pack up to ~A$50 vs ~A$15 under-counter, chop-chop ~A$15/50g. Violence: VicPol link 200+ arson/6 homicides, 500+ arrests but only 107 jailed (Jul2018-Dec2025); ABF Op PRINTWALL >1 kilotonne seized; Combatting Illicit Tobacco Bill 2026 (15yr, 10 Sep). Argument = consumer normalisation — a sin tax set so high it stops deterring and starts creating; the sin-tax version of the curve where a higher rate collects less and creates more. Sceptic = the health gains are real, the 40%-vs->50% spread is wide, the lost-revenue estimate leans on industry-adjacent modelling, the youth figure is a small sample. Under-radar verified (all AU-domestic: ABC, Time Out Sydney, Cancer Council, VicPol, ABF/ATO; no NYT/BBC/Reuters/FT feature). Fresh region (Australia never used). SG parallel drawn (steep duties + duty-unpaid trade) without inventing SG figures.

러닝크루 (running crew) — in the country with the lowest birthrate on earth (~0.7 TFR), a mass 2030-led social institution: ~10m runners (from ~5m in 2017), jogging participation ~23%(2021)→~32%(2023) [Korea Gallup]; sneaker mkt 2.77tn→>4tn won, running shoes >1tn won (~US$730m) 2024 [Euromonitor]; “running” search +82% YoY; Seoul’s official “7979” crew ~300→~1,000 in a year. The “soft community” belonging without family/church/회식 obligation (callback No.80). Two 2026 backlashes: 민폐 public-nuisance war (National Palace Museum notice, Financial News 4 Sep; “전세 낸 것처럼”; SBS/JTBC exposés) and an infidelity/dating panic (PI “sports-club affair” Financial News 7 Sep; viral “break up if they join a running crew” Insight; 애국 헌팅 at Olympic Park, Seoul Shinmun 15 Jun). Argument = Bowling Alone inverted: the most-atomised society rebuilds the commons at dawn, but as a PRODUCT (opt-in/brandable/quittable/obligation-free) — and the friction it engineered out returns anyway (the invoice). Sceptic = infidelity claims are sentiment not survey; marathon 19→254 count and “$1bn industry” are outlet-reported; frame on the Korean meaning not the generic “run clubs = dating apps” trope. Under-radar verified (no NYT/BBC/Reuters/FT feature; Western coverage is the US/UK generic take only). Korea last at 93 (bakery pilgrimage); fresh subject/theme (not idol/luck/cheap-meal/gold/BNPL).

цахим зээл (tsakhim zeel) / "financial fast food" (түргэн хоол) — the app-loan boom that quietly became subsistence credit. In a resource-rich frontier economy the celebrated "financial inclusion" revolution inverted: instant digital loans (gogo.mn calls them the country’s financial "fast food," spreading "like mushrooms after rain") now function as a shock-absorber for a commodity economy that cannot feed its own people. Household debt 42.3% of GDP (IMF Art IV 2025, CR 25/265); consumer loans MNT 11.4tn (~US$3.2bn) end-2024 +35.5% y/y; NBFI credit +54.7% y/y, primarily to individuals; >500 NBFIs (dozens digital) in a country of ~3.5m. Killer stat: >half of pensioners hold pension loans (avg DTI ~84%); for 87.7% of pensioner-borrowers (~250k people) income after repayment falls below the subsistence minimum, and for 40,500 the entire pension services debt — a new rule now forces a subsistence floor. DTI caps tightened 3× in 2yr (70% online 2023 / 50% bank Mar 2025 / 60% NBFI). Food inflation ~2× headline; tugrik ~-45%/decade (held, via Mongolian-media summaries). Impact-investor irony: flagship LendMN raised up to $20m from Lendable + DWM, all branded "inclusion." Argument = financialised subsistence — inclusion sold as leapfrogging becomes borrowing to eat; the tell is not a crash but the regulator quietly ratcheting caps while the world watches the copper. Analogy = Andhra Pradesh 2010 microfinance crisis (celebrated inclusion → app-driven over-lending → emergency ordinance); Mongolia is early on the same arc, regulating before the blow-up. Sceptic = IMF calls debt "still moderate," NPL ~5.2%, much lending genuinely productive (informal MSMEs), and "borrowing to eat" is an interpretation from correlation, not a borrower survey. Under-radar verified (no NYT/BBC/Reuters/FT/CNN/Guardian feature; only IMF/World Bank docs + Mongolian-language press — gogo.mn/montsame/thinkmongol — and a 2017 Forbes LendMN piece). Fresh region (Mongolia never used); off Korea(103)/Australia(102)/India(101)/Taiwan(100).
